narrative.text: Introduces the WHO Classification of Digital Health Interventions v1.0 as a shared taxonomy anchored on discrete digital health functionalities, and presents the full visual overview of interventions grouped across four primary user categories: 1.0 Clients, 2.0 Healthcare Providers, 3.0 Health System Managers, and 4.0 Data Services.

Explains why the classification was created (four primary use cases bridging public health and technical communities where frameworks like COBIT, HL7, and ISO are too specialized) and how Digital Health Interventions (DHIs) link to Health System Challenges (HSCs), System Categories (such as LMIS and EMR), synonyms, and programmatic examples.

Presents Figure 1 illustrating linkages across Health System Challenges, Digital Health Interventions, and System Categories, and outlines how the classification was developed from mTERG and Labrique et al. categorizations, technical consultations, public feedback, and desk reviews, as well as how WHO will periodically update and version it.

Presents the taxonomy of Health System Challenges organized across eight overarching domains: 1 Information (1.1–1.7), 2 Availability (2.1–2.4), 3 Quality (3.1–3.7), 4 Acceptability (4.1–4.2), 5 Utilization (5.1–5.4), 6 Efficiency (6.1–6.5), 7 Cost (7.1–7.4), and 8 Accountability (8.1–8.6).

Lists the 25 ICT System Categories (A through Y, adapted in part from ISO/TR 14639-2:2014)—ranging from census and CRVS systems to EMRs, HMIS, LMIS, shared health records, and telemedicine—followed by five foundational references for the overview section.

Summarizes the taxonomy tree for Group 1.0 (Clients) across seven categories: targeted client communication (1.1.1–1.1.4), untargeted client communication (1.2.1–1.2.2), client-to-client communication (1.3.1), personal health tracking (1.4.1–1.4.3), citizen-based reporting (1.5.1–1.5.2), on-demand information services (1.6.1), and client financial transactions (1.7.1–1.7.3).

Summarizes the taxonomy tree for Group 2.0 (Healthcare Providers) across ten categories: client identification and registration (2.1), client health records (2.2), healthcare provider decision support (2.3), telemedicine (2.4), healthcare provider communication (2.5), referral coordination (2.6), health worker activity planning and scheduling (2.7), healthcare provider training (2.8), prescription and medication management (2.9), and laboratory and diagnostics imaging management (2.10).

Summarizes the taxonomy tree for Group 3.0 (Health System Managers) across seven categories: human resource management (3.1.1–3.1.4), supply chain management (3.2.1–3.2.6), public health event notification (3.3.1), civil registration and vital statistics (3.4.1–3.4.6), health financing (3.5.1–3.5.6), equipment and asset management (3.6.1–3.6.2), and facility management (3.7.1–3.7.2).

Summarizes the taxonomy tree for Group 4.0 (Data Services) across four categories: data collection, management, and use (4.1.1–4.1.4), data coding (4.2.1–4.2.3), location mapping (4.3.1–4.3.4), and data exchange and interoperability (4.4.1).

Details definitions, synonyms, and illustrative project examples for Client interventions under 1.1 Targeted client communication (1.1.1–1.1.4), 1.2 Untargeted client communication (1.2.1–1.2.2), and 1.3 Client-to-client communication (1.3.1).

Details definitions, synonyms, and illustrative project examples for Client interventions under 1.4 Personal health tracking (1.4.1–1.4.3), 1.5 Citizen-based reporting (1.5.1–1.5.2), 1.6 On-demand information services to clients (1.6.1), and 1.7 Client financial transactions (1.7.1–1.7.3).

Details definitions, synonyms, and illustrative project examples for Healthcare Provider interventions under 2.1 Client identification and registration (2.1.1–2.1.2), 2.2 Client health records (2.2.1–2.2.4), and 2.3 Healthcare provider decision support (2.3.1–2.3.3).

Details definitions, synonyms, and illustrative project examples for Healthcare Provider interventions under 2.4 Telemedicine (2.4.1–2.4.4), 2.5 Healthcare provider communication (2.5.1–2.5.5), and 2.6 Referral coordination (2.6.1–2.6.3).

Details definitions, synonyms, and illustrative project examples for Healthcare Provider interventions under 2.7 Scheduling and activity planning (2.7.1–2.7.2), 2.8 Healthcare provider training (2.8.1–2.8.2), 2.9 Prescription and medication management (2.9.1–2.9.3), and 2.10 Laboratory and diagnostics imaging management (2.10.1–2.10.4).

Details definitions, synonyms, and illustrative project examples for Health System Manager interventions under 3.1 Human resource management (3.1.1–3.1.4), 3.2 Supply chain management (3.2.1–3.2.6), and 3.3 Public health event notification (3.3.1).

Details definitions, synonyms, and illustrative project examples for Health System Manager interventions under 3.4 Civil Registration and Vital Statistics (3.4.1–3.4.6), 3.5 Health financing (3.5.1–3.5.6), 3.6 Equipment and asset management (3.6.1–3.6.2), and 3.7 Facility management (3.7.1–3.7.2).

Details definitions, synonyms, and illustrative project examples for Data Services interventions under 4.1 Data collection, management, and use (4.1.1–4.1.4), 4.2 Data coding (4.2.1–4.2.3), 4.3 Location mapping (4.3.1–4.3.4), and 4.4 Data exchange and interoperability (4.4.1).
Lists bibliographic references 1 through 25 supporting the definitions and illustrative project examples of digital health interventions across the classification.

Concludes the numbered reference list with citations 26 through 39 covering pharmaceutical import tracking, birth and death registration, verbal autopsy, mobile health wallets, e-claims, facility registries, labour monitoring, terminology management, and vaccination tracking.

Provides contact information, WHO coordination and contributor acknowledgements, document reference number (WHO/RHR/18.06), Creative Commons CC BY-NC-SA 3.0 IGO licensing terms, suggested citation, and standard WHO disclaimers.
